**DI48** is the ICD-10 diagnosis code for atrial fibrillation, serving as the central diagnostic cornerstone for epidemiological and clinical analysis within the Danish healthcare system's quality improvement frameworks [^src1]. As a foundational concept in the annual reports published by the Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram (RKKP), this specific code is essential for identifying and tracking patients with the condition across national and regional datasets [^src1].

The primary significance of DI48 lies in its use to define the patient populations for the [[databasen-for-atrieflimren-i-danmark|Databasen for Atrieflimren i Danmark]] [^src1]. The code, inclusive of all its subcodes, is utilized to delineate both the incident and prevalent populations [^src1]. For the incident population, the database captures all patients who receive the DI48 diagnosis for the first time within a 10-year lookback period during the reporting timeframe [^src1]. Conversely, the prevalent population includes patients who have been registered with this diagnosis within the 10 years leading up to the start of the reporting period [^src1].

To ensure comprehensive coverage, patients identified by the DI48 code are tracked across multiple clinical registries. The database pulls records from the [[landspatientregisteret|Landspatientregisteret]] (National Patient Register) as well as the practice systems of private cardiologists [^src2]. In these systems, the DI48 code is considered valid whether it is registered as a primary action diagnosis or a secondary contributing diagnosis [^src2]. This robust methodological approach allows the database to monitor critical clinical quality indicators, such as the incidence of heart failure following an atrial fibrillation diagnosis and the adherence to echocardiography standards across Denmark's five regions [^src1].
